# Video preset

The general-purpose video preset — a player, feature bundle, skins, and media for on-demand video

`@videojs/react/video` is the general-purpose preset for on-demand video. It bundles `VideoPlayer`, the `videoFeatures` bundle it is configured with, four skins, and the `Video` media component. See [Presets](../../guides/presets.md) for how presets fit together and how to customize one.

## Import

```tsx
import { Video, VideoPlayer, VideoSkin } from '@videojs/react/video';
import '@videojs/react/video/skin.css';
```

Each skin has its own stylesheet. Import `@videojs/react/video/neutral-skin.css`, `compat-skin.css`, or `scaffold-skin.css` instead when you use `NeutralVideoSkin`, `CompatVideoSkin`, or `ScaffoldVideoSkin`.

## Usage

**App.tsx**

```tsx
import { Video, VideoPlayer, VideoSkin } from '@videojs/react/video';
import '@videojs/react/video/skin.css';

export function App() {
  return (
    <VideoPlayer>
      <VideoSkin>
        <Video src="video.mp4" />
      </VideoSkin>
    </VideoPlayer>
  );
}
```

## Player

`VideoPlayer` is a [`Player`](../components/player.md) created by [`createPlayer`](./create-player.md) with `videoFeatures`. It provides the player store to its descendants and renders no DOM element of its own.

`VideoPlayerProps` types its props:

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Content placed inside the player context: a skin, the media, and your own components. |
| `title` | `string \| null` | The title to display. Takes precedence over the title the media reports; `null` clears your value, so the title falls back to the one the media reports. |
| `poster` | `string \| null` | The poster to display. Takes precedence over the poster the media reports; `null` clears your value, so the poster falls back to the one the media reports. |

`title` and `poster` come from the [metadata feature](./feature-metadata.md#player-inputs).

The preset also exports a `usePlayer` hook typed to `videoFeatures`. Use it from any component inside `VideoPlayer`; see [`usePlayer`](./use-player.md).

## Feature bundle

`videoFeatures` is the array of [features](../../guides/features.md) the player is configured with:

| Feature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`playbackFeature`](./feature-playback.md) | Play/pause state and actions for the player store |
| [`playbackRateFeature`](./feature-playback-rate.md) | Playback speed state and actions for the player store |
| [`qualityFeature`](./feature-quality.md) | Video rendition state and actions for the player store |
| [`audioTrackFeature`](./feature-audio-track.md) | Audio track state and actions for the player store |
| [`volumeFeature`](./feature-volume.md) | Volume level and mute state for the player store |
| [`timeFeature`](./feature-time.md) | Playback position and duration state for the player store |
| [`sourceFeature`](./feature-source.md) | Media source state and actions for the player store |
| [`bufferFeature`](./feature-buffer.md) | Buffered and seekable time range state for the player store |
| [`fullscreenFeature`](./feature-fullscreen.md) | Fullscreen state and actions for the player store |
| [`pipFeature`](./feature-pip.md) | Picture-in-picture state and actions for the player store |
| [`remotePlaybackFeature`](./feature-remote-playback.md) | Remote playback state and actions for the player store |
| [`controlsFeature`](./feature-controls.md) | User activity and controls visibility state for the player store |
| [`textTrackFeature`](./feature-text-tracks.md) | Subtitles, captions, and chapter track state for the player store |
| [`errorFeature`](./feature-error.md) | Media error state and actions for the player store |
| [`metadataFeature`](./feature-metadata.md) | Resolved title and poster values for the player store |

Its type, `VideoFeatures`, is the tuple of those features in order. Import it from the package root:

```tsx
import type { VideoFeatures } from '@videojs/react';
```

To add or remove a feature, pass your own array to `createPlayer`. The skins expect the features they render controls for.

```tsx
import { createPlayer, orientationLockFeature } from '@videojs/react';
import { videoFeatures } from '@videojs/react/video';

const { Player, usePlayer } = createPlayer({
  features: [...videoFeatures, orientationLockFeature],
});
```

## Skins

- [VideoSkin](../components/video-skin.md) — the default skin, with the modern, frosted look.
- [NeutralVideoSkin](../components/video-neutral-skin.md) — the visually lighter variant, closer to a classic control bar.
- [CompatVideoSkin](../components/video-compat-skin.md) — the plain, unbranded variant that avoids newer visual effects, so it looks consistent across browsers.
- [ScaffoldVideoSkin](../components/video-scaffold-skin.md) — the minimally styled variant of Compat, a foundation for your own design.

See [Choose a skin](../../guides/skins.md#choose-a-skin) to compare them.

## Media

The preset exports [`Video`](../components/video.md), which renders a native `<video>`. Swap it for any compatible [media component](../../guides/media-sources.md), such as [`HlsJsVideo`](../components/hlsjs-video.md) for HLS.

## Exports

`@videojs/react/video` exports:

| Export | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `VideoPlayer`, `VideoPlayerProps` | The preconfigured [player](#player). |
| `usePlayer` | The player-store hook, typed to `videoFeatures`. |
| `videoFeatures` | The [feature bundle](#feature-bundle). |
| `VideoSkin`, `VideoSkinProps` | The default [skin](#skins). |
| `NeutralVideoSkin`, `NeutralVideoSkinProps` | The neutral [skin](#skins). |
| `CompatVideoSkin`, `CompatVideoSkinProps` | The compat [skin](#skins). |
| `ScaffoldVideoSkin`, `ScaffoldVideoSkinProps` | The scaffold [skin](#skins). |
| `Video`, `VideoProps` | The [media](#media) component. |

Stylesheets: `@videojs/react/video/skin.css`, `@videojs/react/video/neutral-skin.css`, `@videojs/react/video/compat-skin.css`, and `@videojs/react/video/scaffold-skin.css`.
